title: KV slot smoothing and Churn Quota Controller to reduce fragmentation and GPU OOMs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: KV cache fragmentation and rapid slot churn during bursty continuous-batching workloads cause GPU memory spikes, increased tail latency, and periodic OOMs. This ticket proposes a two-part runtime mechanism: (1) a lightweight slot smoothing layer that regularizes allocation sizes and groups slots into short-lived micro-epochs to limit fragmentation, and (2) a Churn Quota Controller (CQC) that enforces per-stream and per-model quotas on aggressive slot reclaims/relocations to prevent domino-style compaction storms.
background: We observe recurring patterns on multi-tenant hosts: interleaved short and long sequences produce many small KV writes, creating a mosaic of small free holes. Existing background compaction can be expensive and sometimes triggered too late, causing runtime to run out of contiguous memory for new KV segments. Continuous batching amplifies this because the runtime tries to tightly pack many requests with varying prefix lengths. Several prior tickets focused on compaction heuristics and slab schemes, but customers still hit transient OOMs under specific traffic mixes (short chat + long context retrieval).
proposal: Implement a complementary approach that avoids aggressive low-level reshuffling as the first defense. The two components are: 1) Slot Smoothing Layer: a thin allocation shim that bins incoming KV entries into 3 size classes (tiny, medium, wide) but additionally enforces micro-epoch grouping (100ms by default) so that new allocations within an epoch are placed into per-epoch subpools. This reduces interleaving of long-lived and short-lived entries and creates opportunities for cheap epoch-level reclamation. 2) Churn Quota Controller (CQC): a runtime policy actor that tracks relocation/reclaim events per model-route and enforces a moving-window quota (events per second) with prioritized backoff. When quota is exhausted, CQC signals the scheduler to prefer soft-eviction (LRU hint) or to delay compaction, and triggers a fall-back allocation mode (spill-to-disk-backed-buffer) for non-critical models. The controller exposes tunables and can be overridden by Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deploy slot smoothing + CQC to canary pool and show <=50% reduction in small-fragment count metric over 24h under synthetic mixed-workload.
- No increase in median latency >5ms for typical gen workloads.
- Eliminate at least 90% of observed OOM incidents in canary hosts for target workload.
- Unit and integration tests for micro-epoch reclaim, CQC quota exhaustion behavior, and spill mode toggles.
- Documentation (runtime config knobs + recommended defaults) merged to docs site.
implementation_steps: 1) Prototype slot smoothing shim in local runtime branch. 2) Add micro-epoch timers and per-epoch subpool bookkeeping. 3) Implement lightweight epoch reclamation path that avoids global compaction. 4) Add CQC actor with in-memory sliding window counters and adaptive backoff policy. 5) Expose diagnostics and metrics: epoch_id, small_fragment_count, churn_events_{allowed,used}, spill_mode_active. 6) Write unit tests and fuzz small-allocation stress tests. 7) Canary rollout (10 hosts) with synthetic mixed workload for 48h. 8) Iterate on tunables and ship to broader pool.
telemetry: Emit the following metrics to tracing and metrics pipeline: ['kv.epoch_id', 'kv.epoch_allocs', 'kv.small_fragment_count', 'kv.reclaim_events', 'kv.reclaim_failures', 'kv.churn_quota_allowed', 'kv.churn_quota_used', 'kv.spill_mode_entries', 'kv.epoch_reclaim_latency_ms']. Also add per-host histograms for contiguous_free_block_distribution. Wire alerts: alarm when churn_quota_used > churn_quota_allowed for 5m and small_fragment_count increases by >100% over baseline.
rollout_plan:
- Feature gate behind runtime flag 'kv_slot_smoothing=true' and 'kv_churn_quota=enabled'.
- Stage 1: Internal dev cluster smoke tests.
- Stage 2: Canary on 10 GPU hosts with mixed short/long sequence generator for 48h.
- Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 30% of serving fleet with 6h monitoring windows.
- Stage 4: Full rollout if key metrics pass for 72h.
- Provide rollback path: flip feature gates off and trigger drain+soft-evict job to revert per-epoch pools to normal slab allocator state.
notes: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/KV+Slot+Smoothing+and+Churn+Quota+Controller. Prototype branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/eng/kv-smoothing. This approach intentionally favors fast, local reclamation and bounded throttling rather than immediate disruptive compaction across hosts.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Micro-epoch grouping could delay reclamation of genuinely long-lived entries leading to temporary pressure. Mitigation: choose short default epoch (100ms) and adaptive extension when long-lived fraction is high. Risk: CQC may bottleneck throughput for noisy tenants. Mitigation: expose per-tenant override and fall back to spill-mode which trades latency for steadier memory usage. Risk: Additional telemetry overhead. Mitigation: sample metrics (1%) for high-cardinality dimensions.
tests:
- Unit: epoch lifecycle, subpool allocation/return semantics, CQC sliding window correctness.
- Integration: multi-host mixed-workload with deterministic verification of fragmentation metrics.
- Chaos: induce aggressive tiny writes and network flaps to verify graceful degradation and no global compaction storms.
- Performance: measure end-to-end p99 latency and GPU memory high-water mark under 10k req/s synthetic mix.
